rules.rule: Diagnose probable fainting episode following vaccination
rules.problem: BP>=90/60 and pulse<=120 are inverted delayed-column criteria; page says BP is 'briefly low' in fainting, so a patient with transient low BP is excluded. Sudden-onset timing not encoded. 'Fainting episode likely' -> probable is correct.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable anaphylaxis after collapse following vaccination
rules.problem: Structure (collapse AND vaccination AND any of BP<90/60, pulse>120, wheeze, stridor, cough, swelling, rash) is a reasonable reading of 'Treat as anaphylaxis'; page gives a management directive rather than 'likely', so 'probable' is an interpretation; delayed timing window dropped; overlap with the fainting rule is resolved only by the signs.

summary: Most consequential: the fainting rule requires SBP>=90, DBP>=60 and pulse<=120, which are inverted delayed-collapse values; the sudden column says BP is 'briefly low' and pulse 'may be slow', so real fainters can be excluded. Timing (sudden vs delayed, 5-10 min, LOC duration) is not encoded in either diagnosis, so the two rules differ only by signs. The CPR step, management and the Refer-if list are not encoded at all.
